sources.title: Christianity and the peoples of medieval Dagestan
sources.note: University scholarly volume discussing Varachan, Bishop Israel, the 681-682 winter mission, Khazar suzerainty, and Hunnic diplomacy.

sources.title: Huns, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Critical overview showing that Hun was a broad historical label and that Sabir identification remains a problem, not a certainty.

sources.title: Turkic Peoples and Caucasia, Peter B. Golden
sources.note: Academic study of Turkic peoples in the Caucasus, North Caucasian Huns, titles, Khazar relations, and religious terminology.

sources.title: The Conversion of the Khazars to Judaism, Peter B. Golden
sources.note: Brill chapter treating the 682 mission, Alp Ilutuer, Khazar vassalage, elite conversion, and lack of evidence for lasting mass conversion.

sources.title: An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples
sources.note: Scholarly synthesis on the Kingdom of the Huns north of Darband, Varachan, Savirs, Kardost, and the 681 mission.

sources.title: History of the Aghuans: introduction and source criticism
sources.note: Translation introduction explaining the composite Armenian text, clerical viewpoint, manuscripts, language, and limits.

sources.title: History of the Aghuans, Book Two, chapters 36-40
sources.note: Translated narrative of the 681 raid, peace, winter journey, Varachan reception, funeral rites, family claims, and preaching.

sources.title: History of the Aghuans, Book Two, chapters 41-45
sources.note: Translated narrative of Alp Ilutuer, marriage alliance, public assembly, craftspeople, sacred trees, religious coercion, letters, and ambassadors.

sources.title: The History of Caucasian Albania, Movses Dasxuranci
sources.note: Academy-hosted English translation for the core mission narrative and its Classical Armenian textual form.

sources.title: Review of Dowsett, The History of the Caucasian Albanians
sources.note: Royal Asiatic Society review identifying the scholarly translation, scope, and evidentiary setting.

sources.title: Saspirs, Savirs, and Sabirs from the fifth century BCE to eighth century CE
sources.note: Peer-reviewed reconstruction proposing Suvar continuity, Varachan chronology, and the 723 and 737 campaigns; used with attribution because identifications are debated.

sources.title: History of the Savirs/Suvars: Evidence from Archaeology
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeology abstract on Chir-Yurt burials, diverse population, pottery, and the limits of ethnic inference.

sources.title: History of the Caucasus, Volume I
sources.note: University open history covering Caucasian Albania, Arab-Khazar warfare, Darband, sources, and regional political change.

sources.title: Caucasian Albania in Medieval Armenian Sources
sources.note: Academy scholarly volume on the composition, dating, and interpretation of Armenian accounts about Albania and northern neighbors.

sources.title: History of the Church of Caucasian Albania according to Movses
sources.note: Institutional study summarizing the Kingdom of the Huns, debated Sabir identity, Varachan, mobility, and missions.

sources.title: Family Matters: Strategies of Rulers in the Caucasus
sources.note: Peer-reviewed source analysis of kinship, marriage, diplomacy, and the Armenian narrative around Varaz Trdat and the Huns.

sources.title: The Problem of Ritual in Medieval Sources
sources.note: Scholarly volume contextualizing Movses on lament, sword fighting, wrestling, riding, dancing, and source bias.

sources.title: Ethnocultural Heritage of Caucasian Albania
sources.note: Institutional collection discussing frontier food, hospitality, camps, crafts, ritual, and the need to separate reported scenes from universal custom.

sources.title: The Country of the Huns and the Caspian Gates
sources.note: University journal study of the Country of the Huns, Derbent route, religious terms, and source geography.

sources.title: The Arab-Khazar Wars in Medieval Sources
sources.note: University monograph on war chronology, frontier passes, raids, tribute, captives, and the political consequences of the 737 campaign.

sources.title: The Pechenegs: Nomads in the Political and Cultural Landscape
sources.note: Brill scholarly synthesis supplying comparative caution on nomadic polities and the 737 Arab-Khazar breakthrough.

sources.title: Darband: the ancient city, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Archaeological and historical account of the Caspian pass, Sasanian walls, harbor, construction, and frontier movement.

sources.title: Dagh Bary, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Archaeological account of the mountain-wall system, fortresses, garrisons, land, and later cistern evidence.

sources.title: Citadel, Ancient City and Fortress Buildings of Derbent nomination
sources.note: UNESCO dossier on the Derbent corridor, citadel, walls, gates, settlement, and long strategic history.

sources.title: Arran, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Scholarly geography and political history of the southern neighbor that Armenian sources call Aghuania or Caucasian Albania.

sources.title: Caucasus: language contact, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Scholarly overview of exceptional Caucasian linguistic diversity and long multilingual contact.

sources.title: Alans, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Scholarly neighbor profile distinguishing Iranian-speaking Alans from the eastern North Caucasian Hunnic polity.

sources.title: Religious beliefs of the Caspian Dagestan population in the fourth-seventh centuries
sources.note: Academic dissertation record analyzing the 682 mission, Varachan, social groups, ritual, illness beliefs, and source constraints.

sources.title: Medieval Syriac Historians on the Turks
sources.note: Source study of Syriac labels, missionary accounts, and the danger of treating exonyms or stereotypes as transparent identities.

sources.title: Note on Byzantine relations with the Huns in the sixth century
sources.note: Scholarly note on Kardost, books reported in a Hunnic language, possible Sabir context, and uncertain script identification.

proposedOverrides.name: North Caucasian Huns (Kingdom of the Huns)
aliases: Kingdom of the Huns at Varachan
proposedOverrides.summary: North Caucasian polity centered on Varachan, active about 660, tied to Khazar power, and transformed during the Arab-Khazar wars around 737.
